exclude: not map data: the unpacker runs on past the 1024-byte tile layer until its input count runs out, decoding the next entry's packed bytes with this entry's table; nothing reads them and the map is never written back from here

The number of square (9, 29). Game `$B4F0` `bit $39A9` names it because of the BIT-skip idiom: the operand's bytes are the `lda #$39` the code enters at `$B4F1`. On choose_attack's path through the LDA #$50 at $B4EE (api_is_ranged_class at $B4E4 returning carry clear and weapon_rounds at $B4E9 returning 0) the BIT does execute and read this byte, but its flags are replaced before anything tests them (N and Z by LDA #$92 at $1DC4, V by the ADC at $28E5, both on game_msg's path), so its value never matters.

Map code entry 0 (action 0): JMP screen_shake ($044C), the explosion's sound and shaking screen. It returns with the carry that random_byte's last addition left ($24EC), so whether the game redraws the view afterwards ($8872) is left to chance. Class-6 square 0 ($3C4A) runs it: what tile square 2 becomes when the party steps on it. Tile square 2 is the opened door at (28,24)/(29,24): check square 2 (message 48, "This door looks incredibly strong."), opened by Picklock 6, ST 9 or an explosive. The record then makes the square check square 3, run at once on arrival with skill 37 (passed only by a first member holding that marker, Dan Citrine), so for any other party it fails: everybody loses 9 CON (message 51, "As you walk into the room you are caught in the middle of an explosion."), less an armour roll of each member's AC (+$1A) in d6 since flag bit 0 is clear ($A8B2-$A8C5), and remote-change square 9 puts encounters 13 and 14 at (28,26) and (29,26).
the blast; carry left random

Map code entry 1 (action 1): gives a disease to every character in use, all parties and hired NPCs together, not only the party at the door: for records 1 up to records_in_use ($0A), select_character ($0338) makes the record current and the bit for disease n, n = the square's record byte +3, is ORed into its disease byte +$28 through the mask table at $3C7B. Returns carry clear. Class-6 square 1 ($3C4D: 01 0A 03 01) runs it with n = 1, Wasteland Herpes, which stops natural healing (con_heal_one $B854) but costs no CON over time ($B7A6).
